LESSON: WRITING 6.4.1 CREATIVITY WRITING: PICTORIAL COMPOSITIONS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.4: Writing 6.4.1 Creativity Writing: Pictorial Compositions
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 6.4.1 Creativity Writing: Pictorial Compositions, part of Strand 6 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four General.

Key inquiry question: How do we use words to indicate the quantity of countable and uncountable nouns? 1. How do pictures make you feel?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. recognize signs of words and phrases related to the theme,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 6.4.1 Creativity Writing: Pictorial Compositions in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. organise pictures in a logical sequence to write pictorial compositions of about 60-80 on the theme,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 6.4.1 Creativity Writing: Pictorial Compositions in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. write a pictorial composition of about 60- 80 words on the theme for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 6.4.1 Creativity Writing: Pictorial Compositions in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the use of a wide range of pictures to write pictorial compositions on different topics for communication. ● In pairs, learners are guided to watch a captioned video clip or observe a signed demonstration of vocabulary related to the internet. ● In pairs, learners are guided to identify, fingerspell and sign vocabulary related to the internet. ● In pairs, learners are guided to identify pictures from online and offline sources. ● In pairs or groups, learners are guided to pick out common sayings from a text and write them in the exercise books or word processor. ● In pairs, learners are guided to use pictures from online and offline sources to write a pictorial composition of 60-80 words based on the theme. ● Learners are guided to, through signs, discuss pictures in pairs/groups and write pictorial compositions of about 60-80 words. ● In pairs, learners are guided to use sayings to make their compositions interesting. ● In groups, learners are guided to watch a variety of videos related to the theme and write pictorial compositions. ● In groups, learners are guided to generate a wide range of pictures from the internet and write pictorial composition together. 1. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 6.4.1 Creativity Writing: Pictorial Compositions together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: learner collaboratively discusses and uses pictures to write composition based on related themes.

● Digital literacy: Learners seamlessly use digital devices to view pictures online and write compositions.

55

Values:
● Unity: is promoted as the learner collaborates harmoniously with peers in groups to discuss pictures and watch videos related to the theme.

● Respect: is cultivated as the learner engages with peers mutually and accommodates other’s opinion on issues.

Link to other subjects

● The learner is able to relate the concept of pictorial compositions to their learning in Kiswahili.
